hints.content:
We are trying to find a **unit rate**, specifically the number of apples per $1$ tree.

$\dfrac{\blueE{\text{apples}}}{\maroonD{\text{trees}}} = \purpleD{\text{apples per tree}}$

We can compare from the largest to the smallest place value.

###Finding the unit rates

We divide based on the unit rate we want, not the order of the columns in the original table.

Orchard| $\blueE{\text{Total apples}}$  ||  $\maroonD{\text{Apple trees}}$ || $\purpleD{\text{Apples per tree}}$
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
 The #1 Seed |$38{,}614$|$\div$ | $84$|$\approx$|$460$
Sweet and Sour|$33{,}088$ |$\div$ |$78$ | $\approx$|$424$
Apple Valley |$39{,}873$ |$\div$ | $92$|$\approx$| $433$

###Comparing the unit rates

Orchard | Hundreds | Tens | Ones
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
 The #1 Seed | $4$ | $\redE{6}$ | $0$
Sweet and Sour| $4$ | $2$ | $4$
Apple Valley | $4$ | $3$ | $3$

The orchards all have $4$ hundreds of apples per tree, but the #1 Seed has the most tens of apples per tree.

###Conclusion

The #1 Seed has the highest rate of apples per tree.

question.content:
There are three apple orchards. Each orchard has a different number of trees and apples.

Orchard |Apple trees | Total apples
- | :-: | :-:
The  #1 Seed  | $84$ | $38{,}614$
Sweet and Sour | $78$ | $33{,}088$
Apple Valley | $92$ | $39{,}873$

**Which orchard has the highest rate of *apples per tree*?**
